subject: E-Commerce
title: Two-Factor Authentication for Buyers
description: A 60-second lesson on Two-Factor Authentication for Buyers.

hook.text: Accounts with 2FA enabled are 99.9% less likely to be compromised. Most shoppers still don't use it.

buildup.text: 2FA adds a second verification step—usually a phone code or app approval— beyond just a password.

discovery.text: Only 28% of online shoppers use 2FA. The friction of an extra step deters adoption despite the security benefits.

twist.text: Passkeys are replacing 2FA with biometric login. Your face or fingerprint replaces both passwords and codes.

climax.text: Security and convenience rarely align. Passkeys promise both, but adoption requires years of ecosystem change.

punchline.text: 99.9% safer but only 28% use it. Shoppers choose convenience over security.

quiz.question: What percentage of online shoppers use two-factor authentication?
